overall_explanation: Reviewed the staged Rust source against the surrounding manifest module. The new `seal()` path is sound: source stamp is checked before and after the bounded copy (stamp includes dev/ino/size/mtime/ctime), the memfd is created private with CLOEXEC|ALLOW_SEALING|EXEC (rustix 1.1.4 provides `MemfdFlags::EXEC`), WRITE|SHRINK|GROW|SEAL are added and read back with `fcntl_get_seals` and verified via `contains`, and the sealed destination is re-hashed with the existing ELF-identity/size-bounded `files::image_digest` and compared to the inspection-time digest, so any mid-copy source mutation or destination corruption fails closed. Error paths drop both `File` handles via ownership; `copy_bounded` uses `take(limit+1)` and errors past the limit, with sanitized error strings. `SyntheticSealedImage` exposes no getters, Clone, or spawn surface; `Operations` is a private trait so only `KernelOps` is reachable from the public method. Module/export gating stays under `cfg(all(target_os = "linux", feature = "synthetic-fixture"))`, so default builds/tests are unchanged (confirmed by the 3-test default log vs 39-test fixture log). Fault-injection test step ordering (8 boundaries) matches the `prepare` call sequence, and the kernel-denial test asserts EPERM for write/shrink/grow/add-seal plus CLOEXEC on the descriptor. No dependency or lock changes. QA artifacts are evidence-only. No landable defects found; the only non-blocking observation is that `MFD_EXEC` requires Linux ≥ 6.3 (or `vm.memfd_noexec` < 2), which fails closed rather than unsafely.
